nordic:diva:507faf176198a2cc025c.t: This thesis explores the experiential and reflective continuity between waking consciousness and the dreaming state through the lens of Research through Design (RtD) and somaesthetic interaction design. While commercial sleep technologies primarily focus on diagnostic surveillance and retrospective data quantification, this research addresses the "recall gap"—the rapid fragmentation and decay of dream memory upon awakening—by treating the sleeping body as an active channel for mindful somatic interaction. Through the deployment of a Dreamer's Pillowcase cultural probe field study and a longitudinal, 24-hour autobiographical experiment ("24-Hour Reality Loop"), this project investigates how systematic, cross-state sensory cues combined with physical habit formation influence dream recall and nocturnal metacognition. The empirical findings reveal a distinct social and personal desire for dream agency, while isolating the "resleep" period as a highly receptive chronobiological window for sensory dream incorporation. These insights informed the development of The Metacognitive Bridge, a wearable device concept that uses a localized, closed-loop software architecture to deliver non-invasive hybrid haptic-acoustic triggers. This thesis contributes to an alternative paradigm for wearable technology, shifting focus away from data extraction toward low-attention somatic scaffolding, proving that interactive artifacts can create reflective continuity across distinct states of human consciousness.

nordic:diva:5851fe62b476595f928d.t: This project investigates how service design can support rural community efforts to improve internal communication and promote activities. The focus lies on Kalvsvik, a village in southern Sweden, where a group of residents expressed dissatisfaction with the current state of communication. The aim is to bring clarity and structure to this situation, facilitating the development of effective communication channels and strategies among different parties. This process involves engaging with local associations, understanding their challenges, and proposing solutions to develop collaboration. By designing a guide for communication practices, the project seeks to benefit not only Kalvsvik but also other rural communities facing similar issues. The project underscores the importance of good communication in fostering active community participation, which in turn contributes to sustainable rural development.

nordic:diva:64830d7e7846c8b9dacd.t: | i Abstract Standardised internal processes are often introduced to improve efficiency, quality, and coordination in large organisations. However, successful implementation is frequently difficult to achieve, particularly in decentralised and project-based environments where local conditions, multiple professional roles, and competing priorities influence everyday work. This thesis examines the implementation of a standardised design process within a decentralised consultancy organisation operating in the Swedish railway sector. The purpose of the study was to explore organisational factors influencing the successful implementation of a standardised design process within a decentralised consultancy organisation. The study also aimed to identify barriers and enabling conditions related to communication, education, leadership, ownership, follow-up, decentralisation, and organisational culture, as well as practical implications for future implementation initiatives. An exploratory sequential mixed methods design was applied. The study began with a qualitative phase consisting of semi-structured interviews with employees representing different regions, roles, and levels of experience. The findings from the interviews were subsequently used to design a quantitative survey distributed to a broader employee population. This approach enabled both in-depth understanding and broader validation of identified patterns. The findings show that successful implementation was influenced by six organisational factors: communication, education, ownership, followup, decentralisation, and organisational culture. The results indicate that implementation success depended less on the technical design of the process itself and more on the organisational conditions surrounding the change. The study concludes that organisations seeking to implement standardised internal processes should ensure effective communication, practical education, clear ownership, continuous follow-up, an appropriate balance between standardisation and decentralisation, and a supportive organisational culture. The thesis contributes both practical recommendations and empirical insights relevant to process implementation in knowledge-intensive project organisations.

nordic:diva:6490006b5669a01c2e28.t: Folkteatern Gävleborg har sedan 80-talet haft som uppdrag att samverka tillsammans med länets befolkning. Och, som regionalt finansierad länsteater arbetar Folkteatern Gävleborg för att nå ut till den breda publiken och indirekt stärka den sociala hållbarheten. Alla ska kunna ta del av verksamhetens aktiviteter. Samtidigt har verksamheten haft svårt att knyta till sig den ovana teaterpubliken. Syftet med detta examensarbete är att undersöka hur vi kan arbeta för att stärka Folkteatern Gävleborgs roll i samhället genom att knyta till sig nya och oinvigda teaterbesökare, på besökarnas villkor, samtidigt som teatern tillåts att utöva sin specifika konstform. Arbetet inkluderar tjänstedesign som ses ur ett tvärvetenskapligt perspektiv och involverar beteendevetenskap. Genom intervjuer, enkäter och litteraturstudier kunde vi se att den ovana publiken såg teater som någonting spännande och lyxigt, men i vissa fall även tidskrävande och kostsamt. En välarbetad föreställning skulle inte ge den presumtiva besökaren relevans nog att köpa biljett. Det blev därför tydligt att den ovana besökarens preferenser behövde inplementeras tidigt i idéarbetet. Eftersom konstnärlig frihet var grunden och motivationen hos verksamheten, samtidigt som debatten om ”en armlängds avstånd” i det politiska styret diskuterades flitigt, var det av största vikt att detta arbete kom att resultera i ett verktyg som Folkteatern Gävleborg kunde styra och vidareutveckla själva. Resultatet: en förenklad och skräddarsydd tjänstedesignprocess baserad på vår primärdata, kombinerad med beteendevetenskapens Cognitive bias. Detta presenterat i åtta diskussionskort som väcker tankar om den ovana besökarens perspektiv och människans tendens att ta beslut och agera. För att illustrera Folkteatern Gävleborgs verksamhet finns inslag av bilder från deras teaterföreställningar löpande i rapporten. SÖKORD TEATER, TJÄNSTEDESIGN, BETEENDEVETENSKAP, KULTUR, SOCIAL HÅLLBARHET, GÄVLEBORG, COGNITIVE BIAS Figur 2: Föreställningen ”Hjärta av glas” (Van der Kaaij u.å a).

nordic:diva:67f82cd7b8a1d827c371.t: This study explores how climate-related social media communication can be designed to engage young adults within municipal communication contexts. As younger audiences increasingly consume information through fast-paced and visually driven platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, municipalities face challenges in adapting traditional public communication practices to contemporary digital environments. The study investigates how communication strategies related to storytelling, emotional engagement, platform adaptation, gamification, and participatory communication influence young adults’ perceptions of engagement and relevance in climate-related communication. The study applies a qualitative Research Through Design (RtD) approach, combining literature review, qualitative surveys with municipal employees, semi-structured interviews with young adults, thematic analysis, prototype development, and prototype evaluation. Municipal employees contributed insights regarding communication challenges, institutional expectations, and current communication practices, while young adults shared perspectives on social media habits, communication preferences, and engagement with climate-related content. The findings suggest that young adults engage more strongly with communication that is visually engaging, emotionally resonant, platform-adapted, and connected to everyday life. Storytelling, short-form video formats, humour, gamification, and community participation were consistently associated with increased attention, memorability, and willingness to participate in sustainability initiatives. At the same time, participants emphasised the importance of maintaining institutional credibility, transparency, and realistic implementation within municipal communication. Based on these findings, a series of communication prototypes was developed and iteratively refined through participant feedback. The findings and prototype insights were further translated into a practical municipal social media engagement handbook aimed at supporting municipalities in developing more engaging and participatory climate communication strategies for younger audiences. The study contributes insights into how municipalities may combine platform-adapted communication practices with institutional legitimacy within digital communication environments and demonstrates how Research Through Design methods can support communication development within public-sector contexts.

nordic:diva:6da9b11c104344135813.t: The aim with this study is to explore how English as a Foreign Language teachers and teachers-to-be experience participating in a collaborative, practice-based professional learning process focused on supporting students’ willingness to communicate. Specifically, the study investigates whether and how participation in a participatory design process informed by restorative pedagogy supports teachers in developing new approaches to fostering students’ willingness to communicate. The study applies a qualitative action research approach and is built around data in the form of journals, transcripts of a meeting and other collaboratively constructed materials. The project included two teachers and two teachers-to-be who, in accordance with the applied participatory design, shared in creating all of these materials. The findings of the study suggest that being part of a participatory design allowed for a deeper integration of theoretical knowledge into situated practice and compared to previous experiences of professional development activities, participation in this project felt more effortless, natural and educational. The voluntary aspect of the process also gave the participants a sense of agency which was highly beneficial to their willingness and ability to engage and learn. Apart from these findings, several models such as the Dare to Share-model and Participatory Design Circle were constructed during this process that in themselves could be interpreted as valuable contributions to the research field and the participants’ local teaching communities.

nordic:diva:7153034efcc85c66a7f0.t: Denna studie undersöker representation av kvinnliga karaktärer i spel med fördefinierade spelbara karaktärer, med fokus på hero shooters. Tidigare forskning har i stor utsträckning behandlat kvinnlig representation i befintliga spel eller avataranpassning, vilket lämnar en kunskapslucka kring hur kvinnlig representation kan utforskas i spel där spelare väljer mellan färdiga karaktärer. Syftet med studien är att utforska hur självidentifierade kvinnliga spelare konceptualiserar och artikulerar representation av kvinnliga karaktärer i hero shooters genom en participatory design-process. Studien genomfördes genom en workshop där deltagarna skapade kvinnliga karaktärer utifrån en spekulativ designbrief, genomförde en Role on the Wall-övning och presenterade samt diskuterade sina karaktärer. Det insamlade materialet bestod av visuella artefakter, skriftliga anteckningar, presentationer och gruppdiskussioner. Materialet analyserades genom reflexiv tematisk analys. Resultatet visar att deltagarna inte främst konceptualiserade kvinnlig representation som en fråga om yttre utseende, utan genom livserfarenhet, funktionell konsekvens, inre konflikt, variation och reflexiv användning av stereotyper. Utifrån analysen formulerades preliminära riktlinjer för kvinnlig karaktärsdesign, vilka därefter granskades genom 3 separata semistrukturerade intervjuer. Studien bidrar med ett explorativt perspektiv på hur kvinnliga spelare kan involveras som co-designers i utvecklingen av mer varierad och kontextuellt förankrad karaktärsdesign.

nordic:diva:72b3f327e63f7e326ee4.t: What If We Stayed? is a speculative design project exploring how young people can reimagine rural futures in Sweden. In response to rural depopulation, youth out-migration, and disengagement from community development, the project uses participatory methods to involve youth in critical conversations about place, identity, and possibility. Through interviews, workshops, and a custom-designed board game, the project investigates how speculative scenarios and creative tools can empower young people to envision alternative futures for rural living. Grounded in social design theory and sustainability principles, the project frames the designer’s role as a facilitator and co-creator, not a distant expert. The outcome, a speculative future-focused game, serves as both a conversation tool and a participatory research method. It encourages reflection, shared storytelling, and agency among youth, while offering a scalable format for use by educators, planners, and communities. This work affirms the power of design in enabling rural youth to reclaim authorship of the futures they are often excluded from shaping.

nordic:diva:74e5f1fbb91aba2026fc.t: Digital systems are often presented as neutral and universal despite being shaped by hidden assumptions regarding users’ bodies, behaviours, abilities, and needs. This bachelor thesis in Interaction Design, explores how such assumptions become embedded within interaction design and how they influence perceptions of inclusivity, neutrality, and adaptation in digital systems. Through literature research, interviews, user testing, participatory design, and speculative redesigns of systems such as ChatGPT and Google Maps, the project investigated how hidden assumptions manifest within everyday interaction experiences. The redesigned prototypes introduced features focused on transparency, contextual adaptation, safety, and user control. Interestingly, while the original systems were frequently described as “for everyone” or “neutral,” the redesigned versions were often perceived as “more for women” despite being designed to support broader inclusivity and flexibility. This suggested that many assumptions embedded within existing interaction systems may remain invisible precisely because they have become normalized. When redesigns instead attempted to expose, challenge, or adapt beyond these norms, participants became more likely to perceive the systems as targeted toward specific groups rather than universal or neutral. The final outcome of the thesis is a reflective design toolkit aimed at helping interaction designers identify, question, and negotiate hidden assumptions throughout the design process. The toolkit was further explored through the development of a final redesigned ChatGPT prototype informed by participatory testing and reflective design principles. The thesis argues that inclusive interaction design is not solely about adding marginalized users into existing systems, but about critically examining who systems are designed around from the beginning. Through reflective and transparent design approaches, the project explores how interaction design may help reduce the gap between imagined users embedded within systems and the diverse realities of actual human experience.

nordic:diva:76d1a16c16dff2847e58.t: As smart locks become increasingly more common, the need for inclusive and accessible keypad design grows. This thesis investigates how keypad interfaces can be designed to accommodate a diverse range of users, including individuals with varying physical, sensory, and cognitive abilities. The project was conducted on behalf of a company specializing in locks and access systems, the project follows the Double Diamond design process—Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver. Through a combination of literature review, user testing, interviews, and evaluations, the study identifies common usability challenges such as unclear symbols, poor visibility, and insufficient tactile feedback. These insights informed a set of design recommendations, compiled into a handbook and applied to two conceptual product prototypes. The results emphasize the importance of intuitive layouts, clear visual and tactile cues, and responsive feedback. By addressing these aspects, the proposed solutions aim to enhance usability for a broader user base and support the development of more inclusive products.

nordic:diva:7abe05eb8831098f30ca.t: This thesis investigates how Interaction Design can facilitate somatic consciousness of orientation within institutional “straightness” through embodied interaction, ambiguity, and non-normative movement. Drawing on queer phenomenology, somaesthetic interaction design, and Research-through-Design practices, the project explores orientation as a socio-somatic design material shaped through bodily movement, institutional expectations, visibility, and spatial relations. Through participatory workshops, reflective drawings, embodied digital sketching, and responsive sound-based interventions situated within university spaces, participants were encouraged to negotiate movement beyond habitual and efficiency-driven behaviour. The findings suggest that refusing normative movement patterns can provoke hesitation, playful experimentation, and reflection on bodily visibility and socially acceptable behaviour within institutional environments. The thesis offers two connected contributions: first, orientation as a design material for Interaction Design; and second, a social contribution by exploring how design can facilitate somatic consciousness of institutional orientations through embodied and non-normative movement.

nordic:diva:7e53313faecd27ca987a.t: Artificial Intelligence is increasingly being implemented in all areas of technology. This paper explores design ideas for how to implement Artificial Intelligence features seamlessly into a graphical user interface for machine vision, focusing on context awareness to help newer users and on not disrupting experienced users from their established workflow. Throughout the Research through Design process, qualitative data were collected on the workflow and friction points of the graphical user interface by interviewing users at different experience levels, and prototype ideas were iterated and continuously evaluated through workshops with participants who work with the graphical user interface daily. The final prototype included designs for helping novice users choose Analysis Tools and format Result Strings. The prototyped ideas focus on giving recommendations through the use of Large Language Models, based on information in the system documentation and user descriptions of what type of inspection the user wants to perform and what results they want to get out of their inspection. The solution is made with both experienced and novice users in mind, helping newer users without causing frustration in expert users. Important findings were related to ensuring agency, the importance of finding a balance between subtlety and explainability of features, and keeping artificial intelligence features appropriate to the context of the system. This thesis gives a new definition to subtle and calm integration of artificial intelligence, describing it as creating understandable, non-disruptive, and context-aware interaction, instead of features being made as invisible as possible and feeling inherently natural.

nordic:diva:83e446d4210301d782d4.t: Due to climate changes and human impact, the world’s coral reefs are suffering. If nothing is changed, some of the species that rely on the reefs may soon become extinct. To help restore corals and possibly make them more resistant to environmental stress, scientists together with coral restoration workers are working on finding a solution to this problem. One approach is to build structures for corals to grow on. These structures serve two purposes, as they would also provide shelter for fish and invertebrates that used to live in the reef. The structures are often placed on the seabed by divers, which means they need to be easy to handle underwater. While diving it is important to avoid exhaustion since that can quickly increase the risk of running out of air. It is therefore crucial that these structures are designed with a shape and material that is suited for this type of work. This thesis explores how designing these structures centred around the human interaction with them, can make it easier and safer for the restoration workers. This work has also explored the possibilities of integrating a design for sustainability perspective, where a more ecofriendly material was explored along with social and economic sustainability. The project was carried out by an industrial design process based on a research through design approach, where methods such as observation, literature review, material experiments and prototyping were used to develop a concept suited for several stages of the coral restoration work. The result is a modular structure concept adapted for on-site manufacture, transport, underwater assembly and coral planting. The shape of the structure is designed to make the handling easier and safer, this could make the restoration work more efficient in the future. Material experiment shows the potential of a possibly cheaper and more sustainable material option based on a cement-like mixture of lime putty, volcanic ash, sand and salt water. This might partially replace Portland cement in the future This thesis contributes with a human-centred and material-oriented design perspective within the field of coral restoration.

nordic:diva:86f9f5b76f8a200c674e.t: Självständigt arbete inom musiklärarprogrammet inriktning gymnasium Titel: Övning – strategier, resurser och effektivitet ur ett designteoretiskt perspektiv Författare: Bajo Kohring Termin och år: Vårtermin 2016 Kursansvarig institution: Musikhögskolan Ingesund, Karlstads universitet Handledare: Philip Miller Examinator: Ann-­‐Sofie Paulander Detta arbete syftar till att utforska hur övning på fiol kan designas för att den ska kännas meningsfull och effektiv. Studiens forskningsfråga är: Vilka semiotiska resurser använder jag mig av när jag övar terser på fiol? För att undersöka detta har jag under ett år gjort tekniska övningar med hjälp av olika övningsstrategier för att se progressionen i min utvecklingsprocess. Studiens metod är videoobservation och loggboksskrivande och arbetet utgår från ett designteoretiskt perspektiv. Resultatet presenteras i två teman: Semiotiska resurser för dokumentation och Semiotiska resurser för motivation och progression. I diskussionen problematiserar, belyser och jämför jag studiens slutsatser med forskning och litteratur inom området.

nordic:diva:99f08402395365b7ec3d.t: Coordination in healthcare pathways that span multiple services is widely recognised as difficult, yet it is often treated as a problem of missing information or weak communication. Through a service design inquiry into the ADHD and Autism care pathways at Child and Adolescent Psychiatry (BUP) in Region Skåne, this thesis examines how coordination is actually structured and enacted in practice. Following a three-phase Research through Design process, it combines document analysis, ecosystem and stakeholder mapping, contextual interviews, and participatory workshops with a designed response developed through journey mapping, synthesis, prototyping, and stakeholder validation. The central finding is that coordination in these pathways is continuously performed but structurally unsupported: case understanding does not travel reliably across stages, so each actor must reconstruct it from distributed sources, a condition the thesis names reconstruction-dependent coordination. From this analysis it develops a coordination visibility framework and the Case Continuity Protocol, a clinician-facing design proposal that carries case understanding forward across decision points and handovers. The thesis argues that continuity is the appropriate unit of analysis for coordination challenges in extended, multi-actor care pathways.

nordic:diva:9e842e524c43348e81b5.t: Housing in Sweden is becoming increasingly difficult to access, particularly for students, who face rising rents and shrinking living spaces. This master’s thesis investigates what furniture design could look like if the personal living space in Sweden were to decrease significantly over the coming decades. The project combines a design thinking methodology with a speculative design lens to explore plausible future scenarios within a 50-year research horizon, targeting a 20-year design application. The phases in the process were: empathize with students through interviews to understand their relationship to their belongings and living spaces; define future scenarios and design directions through future wheels; ideate possible furniture concepts through brainstorming; prototype the most promising concept through prototypes; and test the concepts and prototypes with users through experience prototyping. These findings inform a speculative scenario in which compact living, currently a temporary condition associated with student life, may become a broadly shared norm. The result is a furniture concept designed for students and their housing, grounded in the principles of circular economy and intended to remain relevant across multiple users and phases of use. The concept challenges the assumption that smaller living requires compromise and short-term ownership, but instead proposes that durability, material expression, and adaptability can make compact living more relevant and desirable. The project contributes a tangible, forward-looking reference point for future work on compact living, adaptive furniture design, and sustainable residential futures in Sweden.

nordic:diva:abcc29c9dbeb6ae96514.t: As digital technologies become more connected to the environment, society, and material world, HCI researchers are called to move beyond anthropocentric perspectives to respond to the complexities of more-than-human design. This thesis proposes a scaffold to support their attunement to the complexities of more-than-human design. Using a qualitative, exploratory approach, this study comprises three phases. In Phase 1, a speculative workshop revealed the challenges HCI researchers face when engaging with more-than-human design. Building on these findings, Phase 2 involved interviews with experts in the field to explore these challenges in greater depth. Finally, in Phase 3, we engaged directly with more-thanhuman design practices through attunement activities, allowing us to personally experience and reflect on these complexities. Key findings revealed the challenges of designing in entangled worlds, as well as the tools and methods researchers use in more-than-human design. The analysis identifies key qualities of attunement, proposing a scaffold composed of three entangled modes: Wondering, Sensing, and Reflecting. These modes foster curiosity, embodied awareness, and critical reflection, helping researchers cultivate relational mindsets. Rather than prescribing solutions, it encourages HCI researchers to stay with complexity and engage responsibly. This work contributes to more caring, interdependent, and sustainable approaches in the field of HCI as well as design education and practice.

nordic:diva:ada7b2dd1ea2ac3190f7.t: Sveriges 290 kommuner har samma uppdrag men väldigt olika förutsättningar när det gäller ekonomi, geografi och demografi. Gemensamt är att de genom den svenska modellen med kommunalt självstyre ska leverera välfärdstjänster av hög kvalitet och förverkliga den politik som medborgarna röstar fram vart fjärde år. Den tid vi lever i innebär stora och komplexa utmaningar. Vissa forskare menar att en grundläggande samhällsomdaning pågår, med nya teknologiska förutsättningar, klimatförändringar och geopolitisk osäkerhet. Statens och kommunernas roll förändras när nya aktörer och former för samhällsstyrning växer fram. Allt detta sammantaget gör att kommuner inte kan lösa sin uppgift på samma sätt som tidigare utan behöver tänka nytt, använda de begränsade resurserna så effektivt som möjligt och på ett demokratifrämjande sätt hitta lösningar för medborgarnas behov. Offensiv kvalitetsutveckling är en viktig kunskapskälla i detta arbete. Med utgångspunkt i denna problembakgrund undersöker studien hur en kommunal förvaltning tar sig an dessa utmaningar genom att arbeta med tjänstedesign som metod för verksamhetsutveckling. De två frågeställningarna som undersöktes var: • Är tjänstedesign en framgångsrik metod för verksamhetsutveckling? • I vilken utsträckning har systematiskt kvalitetsarbete integrerats till en ledningsfråga genom arbetet med tjänstedesign? Studien genomfördes som en kvalitativ fallstudie där tio semistrukturerade intervjuer enligt metoden Appreciative Inquiry genomfördes med sex medarbetare och fyra ledare i en kommunal förvaltning. Resultatet visar att tjänstedesign kan vara en framgångsrik metod för att sätta användaren av välfärdstjänsterna i centrum och för att ge en ökad insikt om användarna och förbättra relationen mellan medborgare och myndighet. Metoden är dock relativt krävande och kräver ett aktivt och kommunicerande ledarskap samt en övergripande styrning och länkning genom hela organisationen där medarbetarnas kunskaper tas tillvara för att stödja en positiv förändringskultur.

nordic:diva:b06d66bdfad649e09ccc.t: Menstruationsgödning är en praktik som innebär att använda menstruationsblod för att göda växter och uppmuntra personer att omfamna sina kroppar, samt att se menstruation som en naturlig och värdefull tillgång snarare än något som ska döljas eller stigmatiseras. Studien syftar till att utforska relationerna mellan menstruerande och växter som gödslas med menstruationsblod, observera perspektiv förändringar i förhållande till kroppsliga vätskor och förbättra självomfamning genom praktik och prototyputveckling. Genom att tillämpa metoden Research through Design (RtD) skapades den spekulativa verktygssamlingen “Blooming Bonds” för att guida menstruerande att utföra menstruationsgödning på ett lämpligt sätt. Detta innebär att förstå växter genom jordnäringsämnen, skapa ett recept för menstruationsgödsel och förbereda gödslet till växterna. Studien inkluderar en tematisk analys av självbiografiska reflektioner kring att utföra menstruationsgödning och använda Blooming Bonds-prototypen under en månads cykel. Diskussionen visar betydande relationer som bildas mellan menstruerande och växter, perspektiv förändringar i förhållande till menstruation och menstruationsblod, samt potentiella områden för framtida forskning, och erbjuder insikter om den transformativa potentialen hos menstruationsgödning för att utmana samhälleliga normer och öka den ekologiska medvetenheten om omsorg bortom sig själv. CCS Concepts: • Human-centered computing →Interaction design.

nordic:diva:bb66cf4d235a6095e1f5.t: Studien syftade till att genom aktionsforskning undersöka hur det kan skapas användbarhet i en e-handelslösning. Bakgrunden till detta ligger i författarnas eget antagande kring att det spelar in fler faktorer än endast användbarhet när ett gränssnitt skall skapas för en webbplats som erbjuder e-handel. Faktorerna identifierades till användbarhet, handlingsbarhet samt teori kring sambandet mellan förtrogenhet, tillit och lojalitet, ur vilka det gjordes ett urval för denna studie. Genom att sätta ihop dessa faktorer skapades en egen designteori, kallad ehandelsbarhet. E-handelsbarhet applicerades på en webbplats med e-handel i syfte att utföra en praktisk omarbetning av ett existerande gränssnitt. Detta utfördes genom heuristisk utvärdering samt en kontrollista och blev därigenom en applicerad designmetod. Utöver detta genomfördes användartester i syfte att empiriskt påvisa att designteorin hittade problem med gränssnittet och därav praktiskt fungerar. Användartester utfördes även för att finna ytterligare problem utöver de som designteorin hittade. Resultatet av den heuristiska utvärderingen och kontrollistan var ett antal problem med gränssnittet. De problem som designteorin samt användartester hittade åtgärdades efter samma designteori och resulterade därigenom i ett förbättrat gränssnitt på e-handelswebbplatsen. Resultatet presenteras i form av statiska mockuper på gränssnittet. Den frågeställning och problemformulering som ställdes uppfylldes via den definition av användbarhet som gjordes utifrån den egna designteorin.

nordic:diva:bc029bf8a8e568e668d8.t: Den välkända linjära Stage-Gate processen har genom åren blivit till en av de vanligaste produktutvecklingsprocesserna för de flesta stora företag inom tillverkningsindustrin. Innovation och teknologi sker i snabb takt och ny teknik utvecklas ständigt vilket innebär att företagen också måste anpassa sig för att fortsätta vara konkurrenskraftiga. De iterativa produktutvecklingsprocesserna har tagit över alltmer under de senaste åren, en av dessa är Design Thinking. Forskning om samexistensen av dessa båda processer inom samma organisation är mycket begränsad, syftet är därför med denna studie att öka kunskapen kring hur företag kan arbeta med integrering av iterativa processer, mer specifikt, Design Thinking i en Stage-Gate process. Studien inleddes med en litteraturstudie där kunskap och förståelse för iterativa och linjära utvecklingsprocesser skapades. Datainsamling med stöttning av denna teoretiska bakgrund genomfördes i form av en intervjustudie där tillämpning av processerna Design Thinking i kombination med Stage-Gate på arbetsplatser undersöktes. Resultatet av intervjustudien analyserades för att besvara frågor kring strategier och tillvägagångssätt för hur och när Design Thinking kan implementeras i en linjär process teoretiskt och praktiskt. I studien har tre internationellt väletablerade företag deltagit, dessa tre företag har tidigare erfarenhet av att arbeta med Design Thinking och valdes till detta projektet då de har tydligt strukturerade arbetsprocesser kopplat till ämnet. Gemensamt för företagen som deltog i studien är att de alla ser vikten att arbeta iterativt i utvecklingsprojekt och att de upplever stora möjligheter i form av bland annat stora tidsbesparingar bara organisationerna vågar investera den tid som krävs för upplärning. De är också enade om att en involverad användare är avgörande för ett lyckat projekt, men att vid implementeringen finns en rad utmaningar som övervinns genom att fatta rätt beslut. Företagen har anpassat Design Thinking och Stage-Gate processerna efter sin bransch och nuvarande processtruktur, vilket resulterat i att denna rapport inte beskriver en generellt anpassad process utan flera alternativa processer.

nordic:diva:c1755f5121d6dff2e85e.t: Voice assistants hold promise for supporting independent living among older adults, but traditional voice assistants rely on rigid turn-taking that fails to accommodate natural speech patterns. While recent research employs large multimodal models to enable fluid conversation, most solutions rely on automatic adaptation which risks perpetuating benevolent paternalism, inadvertently infringing upon user agency by making choices for them. Granting older adults’ manual control also introduces a "double-edged sword": satisfying their psychological need for autonomy while introducing extraneous cognitive load. The present study investigates how older adults with varying sensory and physical abilities experience the tension between autonomy and cognitive burden when customizing the conversational behaviors of a voice assistant powered by a large multimodal model. Adopting Participatory Design, this study shifts older adults from passive subjects to active co-creators. Seven older adults participated in interviews and co-design sessions, using Google Stitch and the ChatGPT application as technology probes to ground abstract concepts of AI customization. Findings recast manual customization as a fundamental accessibility requirement, indicating a narrow window for demonstrating basic usability before technology abandonment. This highlights the necessity of multimodal customization enabled through both voice and a graphical user interface to grant older adults a verifiable degree of control.

nordic:diva:d131fd3a4a4cb428f431.t: Grocery shopping depends strongly on visual information, whether it’s identifying a product, reading ingredients and allergen warnings or checking an expiry date. AI-based visual assistance applications can make some of this information more accessible to blind and visually impaired people, but using these tools in an actual supermarket also brings challenges that aren’t only related to how accurately a product can be recognized. This thesis explores how interaction design can better support blind and visually impaired people in making safe and independent choices while grocery shopping. The research combined an in-store evaluation of three AI visual assistance applications, a contextual inquiry with a blind participant and a digital ethnography of online blind and visually impaired communities. The thematic network analysis identified the following four connected challenges: embodied interaction constraints, unreliable AI output, inaccessible error communication, and recovery being left to the user. These findings showed how users often compensate for technological limitations through physical adaptation, repeated extra verification and their own recovery strategies. A co-design session explored alternative interactions including gesture-based commands, safety-critical information, haptic feedback and guided recovery. These ideas were brought together in a proposed user journey and a low-fidelity prototype. The project suggests that supporting independence requires more than improving AI recognition. Interaction design can make system behaviour clearer, support recovery and reduce the burden placed on users when technology fails or becomes uncertain. The proposed interaction remains exploratory and requires further evaluation with a larger and more diverse group of blind and visually impaired users.

nordic:diva:da74398be7e62cac504a.t: Medieindustrin är beroende av komplexa Business-to-Business (B2B) plattformar för att hantera och distribuera innehåll. Även om dessa system är kritiska har deras gränssnitt historiskt sett fått mindre uppmärksamhet än Business-to-Customer (B2C) produkter, vilket har resulterat i användbarhetsutmaningar som direkt påverkar effektiviteten och introducerar risker vid hantering av känsligt material. Denna studie undersöker hur navigeringen inom ClipSources system Media Center kan förbättras för dess användare. Vidare ger den en reflektion kring hur AI-verktyg kan stödja designprocessen. Genom att använda Research through Design, kombinerat med inslag av Design Thinking för att vägleda den användarcentrerade processen, använder studien semistrukturerade intervjuer, iterativ prototypframtagning, kognitiva genomgångar och utvärdering tillsammans med yrkesverksamma inom medieindustrin. Studien tyder på att effektiv B2B user experience (UX) bör anpassas för både nybörjare och avancerade användare genom en tydlig informationshierarki, inbyggd vägledning och genomtänkt visuell design, snarare än att enbart minimera komplexitet, eftersom användare inom mediebranschen har en relativt hög tolerans för inlärningskurvor. CCS Concepts: • Human-centered computing →User interface design; Usability testing; User studies; Interaction design; Empirical studies in HCI.

nordic:diva:ed7fc0a0a6328668a09d.t: ARTICLE HISTORY Playgrounds are essential for providing for children’s right to play, yet Received 17 January 2025 often contain barriers that affect all children, including those with disabil­ Accepted 30 May 2025 ities. To address these challenges, human rights and standards documents KEYWORDS advocate for inclusive playgrounds using a Universal Design (UD) approach. Universal design; play However, expertise on applying UD to playgrounds remains scarce. space; inclusive Therefore, the current study aimed to identify experts’ experiences and playground; children; strategies for applying UD in playgrounds. Six UD experts were interviewed play; walk and talk using a go-along method at four playgrounds located in Dublin, Ireland. Experts demonstrated a shared understanding of UD, emphasising strat­ egies like adapting environments to children’s diverse needs, fostering teamwork, and creating a positive social atmosphere. Natural elements played a central role, benefiting both children and the community. Importantly, participants did not aim to apply UD to each playground component but to the whole playground environment. In this way, play challenges and social inclusion for diverse users could be maximised.

nordic:diva:efcfcebc49ed82ac6d1c.t: Systems are shaped by dominant mindsets that constrain which futures can be imagined or made possible. Supporting system transformation requires shifting temporal boundaries and revealing the hidden system logics. This study explores how design can contribute to understanding and reframing sociotechnical system change from within. In an empirical study conducted within a research consortium investigating the electrification of road freight transport, we, as design researchers, entered the system change as participants. Using a practice-oriented lens, we learned from riding in trucks, conducting contextual observations, and interviewing drivers and transport planners whose everyday work sustains the system. What is often portrayed as a tightly controlled, planned system instead revealed itself as held together by human skills. This study uncovered how systems are maintained by workarounds – established practices and improvised actions that expose hidden tensions and logics. We propose that workarounds can be used as potential leverage points for transformative change.

nordic:diva:f4fcd88747bff59cff59.t: Johansson, K. 2026. Design for Societal Values. Co-Designing Cultural Interventions with Societal Value Stakeholders. Uppsala Studies in Human-Computer Interaction 8. 142 pp. Uppsala: Uppsala University, Department of Informatics and Media. ISBN 978-91-506-3193-7. Co-design endeavors with representatives from the public sector, NGOs, and other societal value stakeholders are common in social innovation projects. Value considerations are crucial for ensuring that such projects succeed and avoid breakdowns. Yet there is limited HCI research on how societal values are mediated in these collaborations. This thesis investigates this within the domain of designing cultural interventions in public settings. The thesis adopts a Research through Design (RtD) approach, with three main design projects as empirical cases. The projects were followed over several years, from initiation through to implementation, and are analyzed through the lens of how societal values are mediated in design processes. The analysis is structured around three sensitizing constructs: Value Elicitation, Value Translation, and Value Manifestation. The findings show that societal value stakeholders possess high value competence and a strong aptitude for engaging in value conversations, but were unfamiliar with interaction design practices. The study demonstrates that a relational approach, characterized by sustained informal conversations and creative, playful, and reflective methods, lowered prestige, built trust, and enabled complex value discussions. As values became manifested in sketches and prototypes, the value conversations gained increasing granularity. New societal value considerations also emerged throughout the design process and beyond implementation. Designing for societal value mediation was found to require continuous deliberation and interpretative work, rather than relying on fixed design requirements. The thesis contributes insights into co-design with societal value stakeholders in social innovation projects. It positions designers as societal value mediators, both by conceptualizing this role theoretically and by proposing concrete methods for eliciting, translating, and manifesting societal values in the design of cultural interventions in public settings.

nordic:iris:5f0216e068db66833483.t: Design and industry were literally unknown factors in Iceland until the inter−war years. This paper examines furniture as functional objects / artefacts in order to establish in what way this island territory, positioned on the Nordic periphery, was a part of the more centric Scandinavian−design movement during 1950−1970. Based on recent research of archival and visual resources and local furniture collections the paper looks at diverse roles acted out by the Home Industries Movement, local furniture manufacturers, craftsmen and a growing number of urban consumers along with a new profession of architects and furniture designers. It can be argued, in the case of Iceland, that furniture became a material novelty, as well as a leading carrier of memory for design in the early 20th−century rather than the inherent tradition of textiles, carving and metalsmithing, so distinctive of the peasant society. On the other hand Scandinavian design became the most prominent force in the post−war period (1950−1970) and important model in furniture manufacturing during a period of flourishing furniture trade and production where authorship often became an issue. Concluding, in the case of Iceland, that peripheral territories tend to turn to regional – in this event Nordic − rather than global centers as models for local design.

nordic:iris:ab5685f8d81450653c04.t: The design process of prosthetic feet largely depends on an iterative process of prototyping and user testing. As resources for reliable and repeatable user testing are limited, modeling and simulated testing of the design is a positive addition to this process to support further design development between prototyping. The key goal of prosthetic foot design is to mimic the function of the lost limb. A passive spring and damper system can imitate the behavior of an ankle for low level activity, e.g. walking at slow to normal speeds and relatively gentle ascents/descents. In light of this, a variety of constant stiffness prosthetic feet are available on the market that serve their users well. However, when walking at a faster pace and ascending/descending stairs, the function of the physiological ankle is more complex and the muscular activity contributes to the stride in different ways. One of the challenges in prosthetic device design is to achieve the appropriate range of stiffness of the arrangement of joints and spring elements for different tasks, as well as varying loading of the prosthetic device. This calls for an adaptive mechanism that mimics the stiffness characteristics of a physiological foot by applying real-time adaptive control that changes the stiffness reactively according to user’s needs. The goal of this paper is to define the stiffness characteristics of such a device through modeling. A finite element model was made for a well-received prosthetic foot design. The model was then validated by mechanical measurements of the actual product. We further enhanced the model to include a secondary spring/dampener element to provide added flexibility and damping of the ankle joint movement. Reactive control of the secondary element allows the simulated prosthetic foot to adapt the ankle joint to imitate the behavior of the physiological ankle during different activities and in different phases of the gait cycle.

nordic:kgl:06a32b4f734bcaea8cb7.t: This paper describes the approach adopted for developing awareness services in two Webbased collaboration applications, namely CoPe_it! and eLogbook. Both tools are developed in the framework of Palette, a European project which aims at sustaining individual and organizational learning for CoPs (Communities of Practice) by designing, implementing and validating a set of innovative and interoperable Web services using a participatory design approach.

nordic:kgl:13510bdca31f6de855b5.t: Repair remains an underutilised strategy in the circular economy, often deprioritised in favor of recycling despite its potential to reduce environmental impact and extend product lifespans (Keulemans et al., 2023). This systematic literature review investigates how service design can be leveraged to strengthen repair practices. By analysing 60 studies, three key levels of intervention emerge: (1) the micro level, where service design can influence consumer engagement, producer-user interactions, and repair motivations; (2) the meso level, focusing on tools, digital platforms, and process frameworks that facilitate repair accessibility and efficiency; and (3) the macro level, where service design has the potential to shape regulatory frameworks, business models, and cultural shifts that embed repair as a societal norm. Despite its potential, repair is hindered by challenges, such as product complexity (Owen et al., 2024) and insufficient legislative support (Cole & Gnanapragasam, 2017). This review highlights the role of service design in overcoming these barriers by fostering co-creation, developing repair-focused services, and integrating repair into broader sustainability initiatives (Rubenis, 2023). By positioning repair as a service rather than an afterthought, service design could offer new possibilities for circularity and resource efficiency.

nordic:kgl:14229003c0781a0b8511.t: Overproduction in the fashion industry poses a significant challenge, leading to excessive resource use and rapidly growing textile waste before garments reach consumers. The Circular Economy (CE) is gaining recognition as a means to reduce resource consumption through various strategies integrated into product lifecycles. However, effectively scaling these strategies to achieve tangible impacts remains underdeveloped. This paper draws on research projects that collaborate with industry partners to incorporate remanufacturing into existing supply chains. It highlights the essential knowledge exchange required for implementing circular production methods, aiming to identify strategies necessary for scaling. The paper enhances understanding of how remanufacturing preconsumer textiles can be integrated into large-scale fashion business settings. Through two practicebased research projects, one with a major fashion brand and the other with a large garment factory, the research investigates how co-designing pilot projects as a form of knowledge exchange can facilitate the scaling of circular strategies in fashion production. These projects are designed to build capacity, enabling the industry partner to develop systems that can expand the implementation of remanufacturing excess stock. While extensive research exists on circular strategies, there is limited understanding of practical implementation and how collaborations between research and industry can foster a knowledge exchange that supports the transition to circularity. The implementation of remanufacturing, like other circular strategies, depends on adapting processes contextually with a clear understanding of the industry’s existing parameters and developing design responses that can effectively maintain value and recirculate garment stock.

nordic:kgl:15473f8652772c9aa109.t: n Formar ingenieros capaces de afrontar los desafíos del desarrollo sostenible implica integrar la sostenibilidad en cursos técnicos desde una perspectiva aplicada. Si bien el Aprendizaje Basado en Proyectos (ABP) ha mostrado efectividad en la enseñanza de la ingeniería, aún es escasa su articulación explícita con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) en asignaturas como la transferencia de calor. Este estudio de caso implementó un ABP en el curso de Transferencia de Calor II, centrado en el diseño sostenible de equipos térmicos reales, con el fin de mejorar la comprensión disciplinar y fomentar la conciencia ambiental. Participaron 83 estudiantes de ingeniería, quienes diseñaron intercambiadores de calor considerando criterios térmicos, hidráulicos y de sostenibilidad asociados a los ODS. Los resultados fueron evaluados mediante rúbricas técnicas y de sostenibilidad, encuestas de percepción y análisis comparativo con el semestre anterior. Se evidenció que el porcentaje de estudiantes en nivel “Muy bueno” aumentó 22 puntos porcentuales respecto al semestre sin ABP. Además, el 94 % de los estudiantes consideró adecuado el tiempo asignado y el 72 % afirmó haber comprendido profundamente la relación entre transferencia de calor y sostenibilidad. Los hallazgos sugieren que el ABP orientado a problemas técnicos reales y contextualizado con los ODS es una estrategia pedagógica efectiva para fortalecer el aprendizaje profundo, las competencias transversales y la formación de ingenieros comprometidos con los retos globales. Palabras clave: Aprendizaje Basado en Proyectos; transferencia de calor; sostenibilidad; ODS; ingeniería térmica.

nordic:kgl:26499eb8a600871e0888.t: Designing for learning is arguably the key challenge facing education today; new technologies offer a plethora of ways in which learners can interact with rich multimedia, communicate and collaborate. Despite this teachers lack the necessary digital literacy skills to make effective design decisions that are pedagogically informed and make appropriate use of technologies. Learning Design has emerged in the last ten years as a means of addressing this, by providing teachers with guidance and support for their design practices. Learning Design is predicated on three aspects: guidance, visualisation and sharing. The paper will describe the development and evaluation of a new framework for Learning Design, the 7Cs of Learning Design. The framework consists of the following elements: Conceptualise (i.e. what are you designing and why, who are you designing for?), Capture (in terms of capturing resources to be used and activities around Learner Generated Content), Communicate (mechanisms to foster communication), Collaborate (mechanisms to foster collaboration), Consider (activities to promote reflection and enable assessment), Combine (combining the activities to give a holistic overview of the design and associated learning pathways), and Consolidate (in terms of running the design in a real learning context, evaluating, refining and sharing the design). The paper will describe the framework and how it can be used, along with an evaluation of its application in practice. It will conclude by contextualising this work within recent broader developments in the field. The framework can be used by individual teacher or with groups of teachers co-designing learning interventions. The latter has been effectively delivered in a series of workshops we have run over the past year.

nordic:kgl:37514ed809373be04969.t: When considering circular economy, reuse, refurbish and repair of products is key in many circular business models. Both efficient and intuitive disassembly and assembly are crucial facilitators for these strategies, impacting feasibility, cost and economic viability. Thus, product designers and product design educations should focus on how to design products for easy and intuitive disassembly and reassembly to facilitate repairability. The focus from design educations on these specific processes is however very limited. This paper elaborates on the outcomes of a project-based learning course for design engineering students. The students redesigned an electric device (power tool or household appliance) with special attention to design for repairability strategies. Necessary frameworks and tools were offered to first analyze the disassembly and assembly process of the product and secondly redesign for repair. Unlike many other methods that are about assessing assembly and disassembly processes in terms of the time needed to perform them, here special attention was paid to the interactions, both cognitive and physical, during repair. This premise aligns better with the context of end-user repair where time is less relevant but where interactions need to be easier and more intuitive. Through case studies, it was investigated whether this focus generated valuable results and was feasible to implement. The paper is especially relevant for those concerned with circular product design, the assembly and disassembly of products linked to circular strategies such as repair and the integration within design engineering curricula.

nordic:kgl:37ef4ef8108a5fd4b68f.t: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into design education is transforming collaborative learning and creative practice, par­ ticularly in Industrial Design. A theoretical framework was devel­ oped through the literature review to guide this study, which in­ vestigates how AI-assisted tools influence creativity, collaboration, and workflow efficiency in Final Year Projects (FYPs) among 38 Industrial Design students at a Malaysian university. Employing a mixed-methods design, two classes participated in a quasi-experi­ mental comparison: one integrated AI tools throughout the design process, while the other used traditional methods. Students ap­ plied AI tools across five project phases: research (Notion AI, Elic­ it), ideation (DALL·E, MidJourney), design simulation (Fusion 360 AI, Rhino AI), reporting (ChatGPT, Grammarly), and prototyping (generative design tools). Quantitative data from project rubric scores and supervisor evaluations were complemented by qualita­ tive insights from reflective journals and focus group discussions. Results showed that the AI-assisted class achieved higher creativ­ ity and design quality, supported by enhanced efficiency and faster iteration. However, students also reported challenges related to over-reliance on AI, ethical concerns about authorship, and re­ duced hands-on engagement. The study concludes that AI can serve as a valuable cognitive and creative partner in design educa­ tion when integrated within a reflective and human-centered ped­ agogical framework that maintains critical thinking, originality, and ethical responsibility.

nordic:kgl:3d393147373e3b3cc1ad.t: Universal Design has been studied and applied in Education for some decades now, yet it seems still far from becoming a standard in instructional design practices. Teaching educators and prospective teachers how to make a curriculum accessible to students with different needs seems to be a priority, as making instruction more and more accessible and inclusive is relevant in a Networked Learning perspective. The redesign of a blended learning course about Educational Technology to incorporate Universal Design principles is presented here. The participants, who were prospective teachers attending the fourth of a five-year graduate programme, were taught how to introduce Educational Technology in their lesson plans according to some basic principles of Universal Design, while the same principles were actually being used with them. Pre- and post-course survey data show an increase in various aspects, but mainly in the perceived self-efficacy in using Educational Technology, and in performance outcome expectations. The vast majority of participants also stated that the difficulty level of the course was not too distant from their confidence level. Some considerations are finally exposed, about the design challenges that are involved in universally designing a blended learning course.

nordic:kgl:45fe5738e6616308b8fe.t: In this commentary, I discuss how the design thinking concepts of empathy, related worlds, prototyping, ethnography, and story could enhance Ascension Health’s organizational design and ultimately its delivery of healthcare services. When organization design integrates a design thinking lens, more meaningful and innovative processes are developed both internally among organizational actors and externally with end users.

nordic:kgl:49b3df946347ab9593b0.t: Premature obsolescence has significant environmental and socioeconomic impacts. Extending the lifetime of products is a key aim of the Eco-design for Sustainable Product Regulation (ESPR), recently introduced by the European Commission. Several barriers to achieving longer product lifetime have been identified in the literature. By examining the systemic interplay among these barriers and forms of premature obsolescence, we develop a framework to analyse the potential effectiveness of ESPR. Our findings reveal that these barriers are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, confirming the need for public policies that address these interactions and reduce premature obsolescence. Moreover, while the ESPR successfully addresses technical and economic challenges related to product lifetime extension, it remains limited in tackling symbolic obsolescence and ingrained societal consumption patterns.

nordic:kgl:8acc98f1558be11b9134.t: The objective of this paper is to report on the preliminary results concerning the building of the participatory design methodology which is being developed using a participatory approach and supported by the implementation of participatory management in the context of the European project PALETTE. PALETTE integrates computer scientists, educational scientists and members of Communities of Practice with the objective to improve and facilitate the living and functioning of CoPs by developing integrated technological services as well as online learning services. The paper builds upon key elements which were crucial for implementing Participatory Design in PALETTE.

nordic:kgl:a4039838d6c801473c50.t: This paper describes a project that is exploring the development of a learning design methodology. It describes work to date (user consultations, workshops, interviews and resource/tool development) and in particular iterative development of a prototype learning design system, CompendiumLD, to help designers/teachers create and share learning activities. Our goal is to build on recent research on learning design to develop a methodology that provides support to the course design process with an emphasis on the use of technologyenhanced learning. This includes elicitation of current practice in design, identification of relevant resources and development of a prototype learning design tool. We believe it will be of interest and use to individual teachers and course teams, but also others involved in the design process tasked with helping course teams translate their ideas into technical solutions.

nordic:kgl:d1330000988797adca28.t: Although design anthropology, disability studies, and somaesthetics share overlapping concerns, they have rarely been explicitly linked. Each brings distinct strengths— practicality, inclusivity, and theoretical depth—that merit integration. This paper explores how design historically caters to a standardised body, side-lining marginalised bodies as ‘unfit’. By juxtaposing these three frameworks, we argue for a reimagined design ethos that advances social justice through deeper embodiment. Using non-European case studies, we highlight the aesthetic, functional, and political potential of inclusive design grounded in diverse bodily experiences.

nordic:kgl:e80d7e0e3f6dd42da2ff.t: This commentary notes that the authors of the Special Issue propose that organization design knowledge will be more actionable if it is created in collaboration with the organization’s members. I draw attention to a risk in the co-creation of design knowledge: increasing the politicization of the already politically fraught process of organizational design. The reasons why collaborative design-knowledge creation may increase politicking are discussed, and ideas for managing it are suggested.

nordic:kgl:ec2bc3d0526dc2d4af11.t: In order to promote pedagogically informed use of technology, educators need to develop an active, inquisitive, design-oriented mind-set. Design Patterns have been demonstrated as powerful mediators of theory-praxis conversations yet widespread adoption by the practitioner community remains a challenge (Goodyear et al., 2004). Over several years, the authors and their colleagues have facilitated many workshops in which participants shared experiences, captured these as design narratives, extracting design patterns, and applied them to novel teaching challenges represented as design scenarios. This paper analysis the value of design narratives, patterns and scenarios in scaffolding co-design processes in light of previous work in this area.
